chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh, may Allah be pleased with him, told us: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim told us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, Adam (peace be upon him) circled the House for a hundred years without looking at Hawwa, and he wept for Paradise until two great, clamouring rivers of tears formed on his cheeks. Then Jibra'il (peace be upon him) came to him and said: 'May Allah salute you and rejoice you.' When he said: 'May Allah salute you,' his face shone with joy, and he knew that Allah was pleased with him. He said: 'And (may He) rejoice you,' and he smiled. [For] 'rejoice you' means 'make you smile.' He said: Verily, he stood at the Gate of the Ka'ba while his clothes were the skins of camels and cows, and he said: 'O Allah, annul my mistake, forgive my sin, and return me to the home from which You expelled me.' Then Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, said: 'Verily, I have annulled your mistake, forgiven your sin, and I will return you to the home from which I expelled you.'

key_terms.حَيَّاكَ اللَّهُ: May Allah salute you (a greeting indicating pleasure)
key_terms.وَبَيَّاكَ: And may He make you smile/rejoice

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the phrase 'Hayyak Allah wa Bayyak Allah' in the context of Adam's repentance?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* elaborates on Adam’s (AS) penance by depicting his century-long circumambulation of the Ka'ba in humble attire, emphasizing the physical manifestation of his remorse through tears that turned to rivers of blood. It provides a unique linguistic exegesis of Jibra'il’s greeting, interpreting 'Hayyak' as a sign of divine pleasure and 'Bayyak' as an expression of joy, thereby linking the angelic message directly to the restoration of Adam’s spiritual status. This account underscores the Shia emphasis on the Ka'ba as a focal point of early prophetic worship and the profound mercy associated with sincere repentance.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Ali Majilawayh, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by my paternal uncle, Muhammed bin Abi’l-Qasem, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from Abdul-Rahman bin Sayaba, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:

Verily, Adam, peace be upon him, circled around the House a hundred years and did not look at Hawwa’, and he wept for Paradise until it became on his cheeks like two great clamouring rivers of tears. Jibra’eel, peace be upon him, then came to him and said: May Allah salute you and rejoice you. When he said: «May Allah salute you» his face shined of happiness, and he knew that Allah was pleased with him. He said: «and (may He) rejoice you» and he smiled. [1] «May he rejoice you» means: May he make you smile. He said: Verily, he stood at the Gate of the Ka’ba while his clothes were (made of the) skins of camels and cows, and he said: O Allah, annul my mistake, forgive my sin and return me to the home from which You expelled me. Then Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, said: Verily, I have annulled your mistake, forgiven your sin and I will return you to the home from which I expelled you.
